speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you have a chronic cough and have had recurrent bouts of bronchitis; to understand the underlying cause, I need to ask you some specific questions. How many years has your cough been present, and does it persist through the night?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

The history of a chronic productive cough with copious thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for 11 years in a non-smoker is highly suggestive of bronchiectasis. I need to confirm if you have experienced hemoptysis (coughing up blood) or have a known history of tuberculosis or cystic fibrosis. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest
